scope: Private Windows CPU contributors on one physical computer, account and resource domain. Native job containment is tested with disposable processes and actual 32B inference. Independent-host, heterogeneous GPU, public-economic and OS-access-isolation qualification remain open.
validation_notes: All 167 distinct automated cases passed locally. Repeated checks are not counted as additional cases. The actual 32B fault and status-lock campaigns are additional acceptance evidence, not synthetic fixtures.

The application CI job runs three model-independent browser journeys. A separate Windows CI job builds the guardian and runs its four disposable process-tree fixtures without a model. The real 32B campaign and full browser journeys remain local evidence.

An initial browser run failed at pool creation with HTTP 409 without retaining the error body; the last login also failed. The exact original 409 cause was not recovered. A diagnostic repeat passed all ten journeys and observed route availability in all 454 samples. The final full suite also passed after adding bounded real-readiness preconditions and error-code reporting to pool setup. Authentication limits were not raised or bypassed.

The failed attempt placed more than ten login requests within one minute. The configured login limit is ten per minute; the final UI error was consistent with throttling, but its HTTP response was not captured. This is not evidence that a product-level intermittent failure has been conclusively diagnosed.

The existing 27B LM Studio backend had to be restored for browser coverage. Its model bytes were checked against the preserved fingerprint, and its context was set to 8192 rather than the historical 128000. This is functional browser evidence, not a reproduction of the original backend performance or binary fingerprint.

The final extracted-package check verified both current READY/fresh contributors, actual guardian parent/boot bindings, unchanged original private profile fields, the reloaded root, the original local-model node, the rendered 0.11 UI and all nine migration hashes without writes.

The native process-containment binary is a local SHA-256-pinned build. It protects normal contributor descendants, not root/coordinator services, OS file/network access or hardware resource budgets. Windows job nesting can refuse startup; there is no unprotected fallback.
Public fault check labels are selected summaries of the concrete fault records. Historical tags, source packages, migration bytes and F0 sources remain unchanged.

The initial Linux CI build found an unconstrained Result type in the unsupported-platform branch. An explicit Result<(), &'static str> annotation fixes compilation without changing the Windows path. The native parser and all four Windows lifecycle fixtures passed again after this correction. The actual 32B campaigns preceded this type-only correction; installed measured native snapshots and their hashes were preserved. Final CI verifies the corrected release source.
boundaries: one physical Windows CPU host and account, not independent providers
lifecycle containment is not OS access isolation or malicious-work verification
hard-crash session resolution observed at about 35 seconds, not an OS kill-latency guarantee
root/coordinator service ownership, resource limits, service installation and reboot recovery
independent GPU/Linux/WAN/NAT/relay and sustained recovery qualification
independent observed costs, successful economics, approved issuance, public work verification, distributed continuity and cash settlement
